questions.q: A T-SQL developer writes SELECT TOP 10 Name, Amount FROM Opportunity in SOQL and it fails. What's wrong?
options: SOQL has no TOP keyword — the row cap goes in a LIMIT clause at the very end of the query, after ORDER BY
SOQL doesn't support limiting the number of records at all
Opportunity must be written in lowercase
TOP must be written as TOP(10) with parentheses in SOQL
questions.explain: SOQL's LIMIT does the same job as T-SQL's TOP but is written as the last clause of the query, not up front next to SELECT.

questions.q: In SOQL, where does the LIMIT clause go relative to ORDER BY?
options: After ORDER BY, as the final clause (before an optional OFFSET)
Before ORDER BY
LIMIT and ORDER BY cannot be used in the same query
Immediately after SELECT, like T-SQL's TOP
questions.explain: SOQL clause order is fixed: WHERE, then ORDER BY, then LIMIT, then OFFSET.

questions.q: How do ASC and DESC behave in a SOQL ORDER BY clause?
options: Exactly like T-SQL — ascending is the default, DESC reverses it, and multiple fields can be sorted left to right
SOQL only supports ascending sorts
DESC must be written before the field name, not after
SOQL requires ASC or DESC to be specified even when sorting is not needed
questions.explain: ORDER BY in SOQL works identically to T-SQL, including comma-separated multi-field sorts evaluated left to right.

questions.q: What does NULLS LAST do in a SOQL ORDER BY clause, and how does this compare to T-SQL?
options: It's a SOQL-specific option that places records with a null value for that field at the end of the sort — T-SQL doesn't expose this control directly in ORDER BY
It excludes records with null values from the results entirely
It's required syntax in every SOQL ORDER BY clause
It behaves identically to a WHERE field != null filter
questions.explain: NULLS FIRST / NULLS LAST is a genuine SOQL feature for controlling null placement in a sort, which T-SQL's ORDER BY doesn't offer directly.

questions.q: What does OFFSET do when combined with LIMIT in a SOQL query?
options: It skips a specified number of records before the LIMIT cap is applied, useful for paging through results
It sorts the results in reverse order
It limits which fields are returned
It has no effect unless ORDER BY is omitted
questions.explain: OFFSET skips records before LIMIT applies — for example LIMIT 10 OFFSET 20 returns records 21 through 30 in sorted order.
